cards.text: Jesus has just had a long talk at night with Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews (John 3:1-21). After this, Jesus heads out into the Judean countryside with His disciples and spends some time with them there. And He baptizes.
Meanwhile John, who's been baptizing people with water out beyond the Jordan (John 1:26, 28), is baptizing at Aenon near Salim. And people KEEP coming.

cards.question: Why is John baptizing at Aenon near Salim?

answers.text: It is close to the temple
It is near the main road

cards.question: The writer slips in a side note here. At this point, John has already been thrown into prison.

cards.text: Then an argument breaks out between John's disciples and a certain Jew.

cards.question: What's the argument between John's disciples and this man about?

cards.text: So John's disciples go to him and call him Rabbi. They bring up the One who was with John beyond the Jordan, the One John testified about.

cards.question: John's disciples tell him that One, Jesus, is baptizing too. What do they say about the people?

answers.text: Only a few are going to Him
Only His disciples go to Him

cards.text: Everybody's going to Jesus now? When a shiny new stamper took MY spot on the counter, I went quiet in the back of a drawer, but John replies with a line about what a man can receive.

cards.question: John answers that a man can receive only what is given him from ___.
John reminds his disciples of something they heard him say themselves. What was it?

answers.text: I am not the Christ but am sent ahead of Him
I am the Christ but must wait for my time
I am Elijah who was promised long ago

cards.text: Then John paints a wedding picture, and now he's speaking MY language. The bride belongs to the bridegroom, and the friend of the bridegroom stands and listens for him.

cards.question: In John's wedding picture, how does the friend of the bridegroom feel when he hears the bridegroom's voice?
John says that joy of the bridegroom's friend is his own joy, and it is now complete.
So John sums up where he stands next to Jesus: He must ___; I must ___.

cards.text: John keeps going. He talks about two kinds of speakers: the One who comes from above, and the one who is from the earth.

cards.question: John says the one from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks like it. What does he say about the One who comes from heaven?

cards.text: The One from heaven testifies to what He has seen and heard, FIRSTHAND. Not like me back in the junk drawer, guessing what the kitchen was up to from the rattle of the scissors.

cards.question: John says everyone accepts the testimony of the One from heaven.
John adds a line about whoever does accept His testimony. What has that person certified?

answers.text: That he has kept the law
That he is ready to be baptized

cards.text: Why do His words carry so much weight? Because the One whom God has sent speaks the words of God.

cards.question: John says God gives the Spirit without ___.
John says the Father loves the Son but has placed only some things in His hands.

cards.text: Then John lands the whole thing with two roads: believe in the Son, or reject Him. No third lane, friend. Not even a shoulder to pull over on.

cards.question: What does whoever believes in the Son have?
John says whoever rejects the Son will not see life, and the wrath of God remains on him.

findings.problem: The question relies on the preceding story card to identify 'this man' as the certain Jew. Standing alone, it does not identify the other party in the dispute.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The earlier cards give no way to reason out 'heaven' rather than 'his teacher' or 'the crowd.' The baker must guess the unseen final wording of John's line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'His testimony' has no antecedent within the question. The baker must remember earlier cards to know that this means the testimony of the One from heaven.

findings.problem: The setup about speaking God's words does not let the baker reason out 'limit' instead of 'delay' or 'warning.' This asks for the unread final word of the line rather than a meaning supported by the setup.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three period-ended sentences or fragments: the two-roads statement, 'No third lane, friend.' and 'Not even a shoulder to pull over on.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
